Epoch schedule derivation, serialization, deserialization, and slot-to-epoch mapping functions.

# Purpose
This file implements the epoch schedule sysvar logic. It defines functions to build an `fd_epoch_schedule_t`, store it in the sysvar account, and read it back from the account database. The [`fd_sysvar_epoch_schedule_write`](<#fd_sysvar_epoch_schedule_write>), [`fd_sysvar_epoch_schedule_read`](<#fd_sysvar_epoch_schedule_read>), and [`fd_sysvar_epoch_schedule_init`](<#fd_sysvar_epoch_schedule_init>) functions connect the epoch schedule data with the bank, account database, and transaction context. The code also handles bincode encode and decode for the `fd_epoch_schedule_t` type and checks for invalid or missing account state during reads.

The file also provides the core epoch and slot conversion routines used by the runtime. [`fd_epoch_slot_cnt`](<#fd_epoch_slot_cnt>) returns the number of slots in an epoch, including warmup epochs. [`fd_epoch_slot0`](<#fd_epoch_slot0>) returns the first slot of an epoch. [`fd_slot_to_epoch`](<#fd_slot_to_epoch>) maps a slot to its epoch and optional offset, and [`fd_slot_to_leader_schedule_epoch`](<#fd_slot_to_leader_schedule_epoch>) maps a slot to the leader schedule epoch. These functions implement the epoch schedule rules used by Solana-compatible logic, including warmup behavior and leader schedule offsets.
